thread:
oncall-bot: Pager SEV2 — sudden memory blowups on kv-cache workers in us-west-2. 15+ OOMs in the last 3m, latency spikes to 2.5s for inference, increased 5xxs. Tagging oncall: @alex

alex: seeing the same in metrics. heap/allocator delta huge on hosts kv-uw2-*. Memory footprint climbs slowly then drops with process restart.

maria: looks like continuous batching got a new default rollout this morning (batching config v2). Recent canary shows increased average batch token windows. Could be causing longer-lived KV entries and fragmentation.

jamal: confirmed logs show repeated cuda malloc failures and then python process restarts:
```
RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 256.00 MiB (GPU 0; 31.75 GiB total, 29.90 GiB already allocated)
Stack: /opt/redwood/serve/runtime/kv_cache.py:line 214
```

lisa: also seeing many slab alloc warnings from the allocator: "Arena fragmentation > 85%" in /var/log/runtime/allocator.log

priyanka: customer impact — 3 dedicated customers in us-west-2 reporting high latency, one saw 10% error rate increase last 10m. CS notified.

maria: immediate mitigation plan: 1) roll batch config back to conservative values (max_batch_tokens=1024 -> 256, max_batch_size 64 -> 16, batch_delay_ms 20 -> 5) 2) set MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=4 on affected hosts 3) deploy PyTorch allocator tuning: export PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:64 4) enable temporary canary fallback to smaller model variant (redwood-small) for Dedicated customers in the affected subpool.

alex: executing step 1 now — creating hotfix patch to batch config and triggering a rolling restart of the us-west-2 worker pool (canary first).

deploy-bot: deploy started by alex — change-id: DPL-8932, target: kv-worker-pool/us-west-2, mode: canary(5%).

jamal: running a quick script to set MALLOC_ARENA_MAX on nodes (systemd override). Script:
```bash
for host in $(hosts --tag kv-uw2); do ssh $host sudo mkdir -p /etc/systemd/system/runtime.service.d && sudo tee /etc/systemd/system/runtime.service.d/env.conf <<EOF
[Service]
Environment=MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=4
EOF
sudo systemctl daemon-reload && sudo systemctl restart runtime.service || echo "restart failed $host"
done
```

lisa: will also push a config to set PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF for the runtime process. Doing that in parallel.

maria: canary metrics are looking better after first batch change: allocator RSS down ~30% on canary nodes, cuda mem allocated curves are smoother. Latency back to ~350ms on canary.

priyanka: CS updated customers: we told them we’re rolling a hotfix and may fall back to smaller models if needed. Only one customer has requested immediate rollback to older config — they accepted fallback to redwood-small.

alex: canary to 25% now. Monitoring heap fragmentation and 5xxs. If no regression in 10m, continue rollout.

deploy-bot: canary advanced to 25% by alex — change-id: DPL-8932.

jamal: pushed MALLOC_ARENA_MAX and PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF on 12/16 nodes. Restart succeeded for 10 nodes, 2 had restart failures (ssh timeout). Investigating.

lisa: quick note: `torch.cuda.empty_cache()` won't avoid allocator fragmentation — it's helpful between large allocations but doesn't return GPU memory to OS. Real fix is fewer long-lived allocations and smarter splitting (max_split_size_mb helps).

maria: agree. Longer-term: we need workload-aware batching (max tokens per batch + TTL for KV entries) and re-evaluate arena sizing for our allocator. Opened an RFC: PERF-1274.

alex: rollout to 100% complete. All nodes now on hotfix config except the 2 that failed; they’re on manual hold.

deploy-bot: deploy finished — change-id: DPL-8932 status: success (partial hold: 2 nodes).

maria: post-deploy status: 5xxs down to baseline, latency for most customers back to normal, allocator fragmentation metrics dropped from 82% -> 28% average. CUDA OOMs stopped.

priyanka: customer-ops: two customers still flagged for elevated latency; both routed to smaller model fallback. Customer communications scheduled (email + slack).

jamal: follow-ups: 1) triage the 2 nodes that failed to restart — suspected ssh/key rotation mismatch 2) reproduce fragmentation in staging with load generator 3) expedite arena-tuning patch to runtime to allow dynamic MALLOC_ARENA_MAX via feature flag 4) add alert for continuous-batching delta > 15% change in 5m window.

lisa: I've attached quick commands for reproducing alloc pattern in staging: run the batched load with token skew and long KV lifetime. Sharing in #eng-runtime.

alex: passing to night oncall @maria for handoff — everything stable but keep the on-call rotation informed and CS looped in.

maria: taking handoff. Current severity: SEV2 -> downgraded to SEV3. Actions outstanding: monitor the two failed nodes, run fragmentation replay in staging, and schedule a dedicated postmortem in 24h. If any OOMs reappear, escalate immediately.

oncall-bot: Handoff recorded: from alex to maria. Next oncall: jamal (in 6h).

customer-ops: noted — we’ll send follow-up with root-cause summary after postmortem.

alex: thanks everyone — great quick coordination. :thumbsup:

oncall-bot: Pager closed at 1792007921 — status: mitigated, rollback not required, monitoring.
